title: Scripture opened (Dei Verbum)
hookLine: easy access to the Bible for all the faithful

lines: A BIBLE ON A HIGH SHELF.
cards: Some families have one: a heavy Bible with a gold edge, kept on a high shelf or in a drawer. Inside the front cover, in different handwritings: births, weddings, baptisms, deaths. The book records the family.

The question is whether the family ever reads the book. The Second Vatican Council wrote a whole constitution about God's word, and near the end of it, it said something blunt about who the Bible is for.

teach.b: The constitution is called Dei Verbum, the word of God.

Start with the picture at its heart: in scripture, it says, God speaks to people as friends, out of the abundance of his love, and lives among them to invite them into his company. Not a rulebook first. A conversation.

Dei Verbum says the Church has always honored the scriptures as she honors the Lord's own Body, and that at the liturgy she offers the faithful the bread of life from one table, the table of God's word and of Christ's Body.
In a Catholic church, the lectern and the altar stand in the same sanctuary for a reason. Third, the blunt part.
Easy access to sacred scripture, the council says, should be open to all the Christian faithful.
It asks for good translations into different languages, made from the original texts, and says they can even be made together with other Christians, where that's possible.
And it urges all the faithful to read often, quoting Saint Jerome: ignorance of the scriptures is ignorance of Christ. Fourth, how to read.
Prayer should go with the reading, the council says, borrowing a thought from Saint Ambrose: we speak to God when we pray, and we hear him when we read.
Saint Paul wrote to Timothy, in the Douay-Rheims, "All scripture, inspired of God, is profitable to teach, to reprove, to correct, to instruct in justice."

how: Catholics hear readings from scripture at every Mass, and some also read the Bible at home, pray with it through lectio divina, or join parish Bible studies, as Dei Verbum encouraged.

o: the reading that opens every Catholic Mass
the council's call for easy Bible access for all

games.q: a family's Bible sits on a high shelf, used only to record births and deaths. what does Dei Verbum ask of them?
o: leave the reading to the priest.
games.why: the council urged all the faithful to read scripture often, and to let prayer go with the reading.

practice: Open a Bible anywhere in the Gospels, or use a phone, and read a few verses slowly, stopping at the first line that catches. Stay with that line for the rest of the sit.
If you pray, answer it in your own words, the way you'd answer a friend.

wordCard.voice: Scripture opened. Dei Verbum's call for easy access to the Bible for all the faithful, read often and with prayer. Today's words.

carryVoice: Your line: open the book. The family Bible is for reading, not only for records. Until tomorrow.
